chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions who said:

I was present with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and Harun the Caliph, and Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya, in Medina. They had come to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So Harun said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Harun proceeded, greeted, and stood to the side.

And Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Isa proceeded, greeted, and stood with Harun. Then Ja'far said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Ja'far proceeded, greeted, and stood with Harun.

And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) proceeded, so he said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father! I ask Allah, Who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided through you, that He send blessings upon you.'
So Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he said?' He said, 'Yes'. So Harun said, 'I testify that he is truly his father.'

key_terms.أَبَاهْ: O my father (a term of lineage and affection used by the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn Musa (as) say to the Prophet at his grave that convinced Caliph Harun al-Rashid of his lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam's deliberate humility and distinct spiritual status by declining to precede the Caliph, thereby emphasizing that his connection to the Prophet is ontological rather than merely ceremonial. The specific address 'Ya Abah' (O my father) underscores the Shia doctrine of the Imam as the true inheritor of the Prophet's spiritual and physical lineage, a point Harun al-Rashid immediately recognized as divine truth. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for the Imam's unique authority and his role as the living continuation of the Prophetic mission.
